title: Waiting for the Retest
hook: BOS #3 activates the zone. The retest is where the entry lives.

launchpad.outcome: Wait for price to return to an active zone, spot the retest, and recognize a missed retest as a no-trade outcome.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What do you do when price never comes back?

takeaways: After BOS #3, wait for price to return to the zone.
The retest is the first return to the active zone after BOS #3.
Don’t chase. A missed retest is a missed trade, not a trade.
The entry options (a limit at the near edge, or a directional close out of the zone) still need Dayli’s confirmation.

slides.headline: BOS #3 printed. Now you wait.
slides.line: The zone is active. The next step is patience: price has to come back to it.

cards.label: Wait
cards.sub: After BOS (break of structure) #3, wait for price to return to the zone.

cards.label: Don’t chase
cards.sub: If price runs away without returning, you let it go.

cards.label: Missed isn’t a trade
cards.sub: A missed retest is a missed trade. It’s a no-trade outcome.

slides.headline: Where does price come back?
slides.line: Bullish example. The demand zone is active. Find the first candle that returns to it.
slides.why: That’s the first candle after BOS #3 to trade back into the active zone.

after.caption: The retest. Price returned to the active zone. Only now does the entry model apply.

slides.headline: Two documented ways to enter.
slides.line: Both are part of the documented model. Neither is finalized yet.

steps.caption: Limit entry. A predetermined limit sits at the near edge of the zone: the high of this demand zone.
Close out of the zone. The model also documents a directional candle close out of the zone as an extra-confirmation option. Here, a bullish candle closes back above the zone.

slides.headline: Active zone. Price never returns.
slides.line: Bearish example. BOS #3 has activated the supply zone. Watch what price does.

steps.caption: Sellers keep pushing lower. Price pulls back a little, but it never returns to the supply zone.

check.prompt: Price is running away from the zone. What do you do?

options.label: Sell at market so you don’t miss it
options.feedback: Don’t chase price when it fails to return. A missed retest is not an executed trade.

options.label: Let it go. No retest, no trade.
options.why: Right. The sequence completed, but price never came back. That’s a missed trade, and a valid no-trade decision.

slides.headline: Which one is a trade?
slides.line: Both started with the same full sequence.

check.prompt: Both charts printed BOS #3. Which one reaches the entry model?

options.label: Price ran away, so you entered late, far from the zone
options.feedback: That’s chasing. If price doesn’t return to the zone, there is no entry.

options.label: Price returned to the active zone
options.why: Right. After BOS #3, the entry model only applies when price returns to the zone.

slides.quote: The zone waits for price. You wait for the zone.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what do you do after BOS #3, and what happens if price never returns?
slides.modelAnswer: After BOS #3 activates the zone, I wait for price to return to it. The retest is the first return to the active zone. The documented entry options are a limit at the near edge of the zone or a directional candle close out of the zone, and both still need Dayli’s confirmation. If price never comes back, I don’t chase it. A missed retest is a missed trade, not a trade.
